edges.description: N-terminal-domain missense alleles lower the turnover of an otherwise folded enzyme.
Catalytic-core missense and truncating alleles produce misfolded, aggregation-prone or absent enzyme.
Lower turnover per enzyme molecule reduces the supply of charged tRNA-Gln.
Misfolded, aggregated or degraded enzyme contributes no aminoacylation activity.

Insufficient GlnRS activity during brain development is followed by cell death and reduced brain size in the zebrafish loss-of-function model; the intervening translational step is inferred rather than measured.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is damage to both QARS1 alleles. The published allelic series is mostly missense, distributed across the N-terminal domain (p.Gly45Val, p.Tyr57His), the catalytic core (p.Arg403Trp, p.Arg515Trp, p.Val476Ile, p.Arg378His) and the anticodon-binding domain (p.Gln742His), together with truncating alleles (p.Lys496*, p.Arg463*). In the founding families each patient combined one N-terminal-domain allele with one catalytic-core allele.

nodes.description: Both allele classes converge on a reduced capacity to charge tRNA-Gln with glutamine. Because GlnRS is the only cytosolic enzyme for this step, the deficit limits glutamine incorporation into all cytosolically translated proteins. Reduced aminoacylation has been measured in patient cell lines and in patient fibroblasts, including in the milder growth-failure phenotype. QARS1 is highly expressed in the developing fetal cerebral cortex. Why a ubiquitous housekeeping defect falls hardest on the developing brain is not established; the high translational demand of brain growth is the usual explanation, but no QARS1 study measures translation directly.

nodes.description: The catalytic-core variants p.Arg403Trp and p.Arg515Trp abolish aminoacylation activity in vitro and render the enzyme poorly soluble; recombinant mutant protein co-purifies with the bacterial chaperonin GroEL and degrades when separated from it. p.Arg403Trp also disrupts the interaction of QARS1 with RARS1 in the multisynthetase complex. The truncating allele p.Lys496* gives diminished, aggregated protein when expressed in neuroblastoma cells. Milder alleles (p.Arg378Cys, p.Arg525Gln) reduce solubility with little loss of catalytic efficiency, which places the severity of a genotype on the residual soluble, active enzyme it leaves.
